newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH GOVT WINS VOTE OF CONFIDENCE IN PARLIAMENT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH GOVT WINS VOTE OF CONFIDENCE IN PARLIAMENT.

text.p: The Finnish government on Tuesday won a vote of confidence in parliament, the Speaker said.

In the vote, which followed an interpellation debate about the government's economic policy and efforts to reduce unemployment, 121 MPs supported Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's left-right-green coalition, 54 were against, two abstained and 22 MPs were not present, the Speaker said.
The parliamentary groups of the five cabinet parties have a comfortable majority; 142 seats in the 200-member single-chamber legislature where the Speaker does not vote.
The government had been widely expected to win the confidence vote, its fourth since taking office in April 1995.
